review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–128). It declares no @[simp] lemmas, simp sets or simp-normal-form definitions. Its declarations are three private existence theorems, `exists_homogeneous_mem_notMem`, `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_notMem` and `exists_homogeneous_pos_mem_forall_notMem`, plus the final `solution`. All of them are existential statements, so none is a sensible simp lemma, and adding simp attributes to them would be unjustified. The only simp calls are inside proofs. They are `simpa using p.sub_mem hz h1`, which relies on `add_sub_cancel`-style normalisation, `by simp; exact fun p _ => p.isHomogeneous` in `solution`, and `by simp` for the empty-set case. These are proof-style choices, not defects in a simp interface. I found no unwanted expansion, orientation problem, competing rules or cycle that I could support from the sources. I did not open the Mathlib sources to look for competing simp rules. The only uncertainty is that the `p2m_export` and `p2m_open` macros come from P2M.Util, which I did not inspect, and they might add attributes.
